issues.description: The template implementation of simulate_ghz_state in tensor_networks.py has a signature simulate_ghz_state(num_qubits: int) (no shots parameter) but both the problem statement and the reference solution expect simulate_ghz_state to accept (num_qubits, shots). The template function's docstring and body also reference a shots parameter (e.g., asserting shots > 0), which is undefined in the template signature. This mismatch will prevent students from implementing and testing the GHZ simulation as specified and is inconsistent with the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template function signature to include the shots parameter to match the specification and solution: def simulate_ghz_state(num_qubits: int, shots: int) -> dict[str, int]:. Ensure the function body uses the shots parameter (and the asserts/docstring reflect it). This keeps the template consistent with the problem statement and the reference implementation.

issues.description: The problem statement and solution expect the GHZ simulation entry point to accept both num_qubits and shots (simulate_ghz_state(num_qubits, shots)), but the template's tensor_networks.py defines simulate_ghz_state with only a single parameter (num_qubits). This API/identifier mismatch (presence/absence of the shots parameter) creates confusion for students implementing the exercise and prevents a direct mapping from the problem requirements to the template scaffold. The solution implements and tests the two-argument form, so the template's single-argument signature is inconsistent and likely unintentional.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template's simulate_ghz_state signature to include the shots parameter (def simulate_ghz_state(num_qubits: int, shots: int) -> dict[str, int]:), update its docstring and body to accept and use shots, and ensure consistency with the problem statement and the solution implementation.
